## 963dad37593d

**Finding: header position is fixed, permitting a left-prefix shortcut that contradicts canonical data.** `generate()` always paints the rank as `rank` contiguous blue cells starting at column 0 (`g[0][0:rank] = 1`). A rival can therefore read “length of the leading blue prefix” instead of counting blue cells anywhere in row 0 and will fit every generated lesson.

The canonical test is already an exact counterexample: its header begins `[0,0,1,0,...]`. The intended rank is 1 and selects the largest body object; the leading-prefix rival reads 0/no target. Canonical training example 2 also shifts its three blue cells right by one column. The proposed generator should randomize header positions (and preferably include noncontiguous placements) while preserving the count, then add a witness that count-based and prefix/position-based decoders disagree.

## 963dad37593d

**Current-source reproduction; audited source unchanged. A1-D1: fixed left-prefix header creates a generated-only shortcut that a canonical pair refutes. A1-O1: advertised controls and rank bounds drift from actual generation.** Identity: generator SHA-256 `e5207a349a9fb541e5436005a192f893597a320888a1510c0f6f9d8ff7b3080f`; executed canonical rule hash `25920db90e23`; rule-text SHA-256 `a7343e2a98b7bd122e09e6e659475d57137f7c2d002e61d33cda6496a052b2e8`.

### A1-D1 — header placement permits a leading-prefix rank decoder

`generate()` always paints the `rank` blue cells contiguously from column 0. Across seeds 0–19, sample index 0, and easy/medium/hard, **60/60 unique normal inputs** passed `self_check`; in **60/60**, the count of all blue cells equalled the length of the leading blue prefix, and a rival that uses only that prefix selected exactly the same crop as executed Racket. Thus generated lessons do not distinguish “count blue anywhere in row 0” from “measure the left prefix.”

The current canonical training witness at variant 0, train pair 1 passes `self_check` but places its three blue cells at columns `[1,2,3]`. The intended rank is 3; the prefix rival reads 0 and returns no crop. Executed Racket exactly matches the canonical label and disagrees with the rival. `checks/audit/963dad37593d/counterexample.json` retains the exact input, label, authority output, header positions, and rival result. `summary.json`, `cases.json`, and `racket.json` retain denominators and all 61 executed cases.

Recommended follow-up: randomize header positions, including noncontiguous placements, while preserving the blue count; add a task-semantic witness that fires when total-count and prefix/position decoders disagree. Preserve the current left-prefix texture as one case rather than the only case.

### A1-O1 — observable control and metadata drift

At seed 0, sample index 0, medium difficulty, exact `grid_h` overrides 9 and 16 and `grid_w` overrides 10 and 18 produced **4/4 grids identical** to the unoverridden baseline. The four advertised `palette_kind` values and the four helpful `texture` aliases likewise produced **8/8 identical grids**. Source inspection agrees: generation draws `height`/`width`, not `grid_h`/`grid_w`, and does not consume helpful palette/texture values. Separately, `AXES.rank` advertises `1..3`, but 100 hard defaults produced rank 4 or 5 in **33/100** cases. Evidence is in `checks/audit/963dad37593d/overrides.json` and `summary.json`.

Recommended follow-up: bind documented axes to the names actually drawn, implement observable palette/texture behavior or remove those claims, and align the advertised rank range with hard-band output. This is a control-contract and metadata defect; no Racket label mismatch is claimed.

Limits: this was a bounded findings-only audit, not a full battery or lesson census. The measured prefix rival is claimed to fit the sampled generated support, not every possible external input or all canonical pairs.
